fixes.explanation: Milk it is! Peter says, “Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk…” A newborn doesn't need to be talked into wanting it, and that's the picture Peter picks. The milk has a purpose too: “…so that by it you may grow up in your salvation…”
You got it, baker. Peter says to crave the milk “…so that by it you may grow up in your salvation…” Newborns don't stay newborns, and that's the whole idea. The growing comes by the milk.

Chosen and precious, that's the one. Peter says the living stone is “…rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight…” Men rejected Him, but in God's sight He is chosen and precious. I know a little about being shoved to the back of a junk drawer and then called out of it, and it's a very good feeling.

Hidden and waiting sounds like a mystery novel, but it's not what Peter says. He says the living stone is “…rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight…” Men rejected the stone, and in God's sight it is chosen and precious.

A spiritual house, you got it! Peter says the believers, “…like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house…” In Peter's picture, believers aren't stones sitting in a pile. They're being built into a building.

Priesthood! Peter says the living stones are being built “…to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” The house comes with a job attached. The job is offering spiritual sacrifices to God.

A choir would be a nice sound, but Peter doesn't say choir here. He says the living stones are being built “…to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices…” It's a priesthood, and that's the group doing the offering.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, so I get it. But Peter says the sacrifices are “…acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” The person in this verse is Jesus. He's the one Peter names.

Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), is a big name, I'll give you that. But Peter says the sacrifices are “…acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” Peter names Jesus here, and nobody else. Keep that name close, friend.
That would be quite a promise, but the Scripture doesn't say it. It says, “…the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.” Shame is the thing that's promised away.

Ooh, that one sounds fair, but it's not Peter's reason, friend. He says, “They stumble because they disobey the word…” The reason is sitting right there in the verse, no detective work needed. Warnings never come up at all.

A people for God's own possession, you got it. Peter says, “But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession…” Look at that list. Every title is one more way of saying the believers belong to Him.

Light is the word. Peter says God “…called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.” Out of the dark and into the light. I know a little something about stepping out of the dark myself, after years in the back of a junk drawer until an angel called me out.
True! Peter says, “Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God…” That's a before and an after in one sentence. Peter puts the "once" and the "now" side by side.

Mercy, that's the one. Peter says, “once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.” That's a before and after worth sticking on the cookie box. Once it hadn't been received, and now it has.

Strength is a good thing to want, but that's not the word. Peter says, “once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.” I'd sign up for extra strength on a long bake day, but this before and after names just one thing.
